prompt: Explain why the gradient of a secant (a straight line joining two separate points) on a curved displacement-time graph gives the average velocity, whereas the gradient of a tangent at a point gives the instantaneous velocity.

mark_scheme.criterion: States that a secant divides the total displacement change by the total time interval over that period (average velocity = Delta s / Delta t).
States that a tangent gives the rate of change of displacement at one specific instant in time (instantaneous velocity).

hints: What does a secant measure across a time interval?
What does a tangent line touch at a single instant?
solution: A secant connects two separate points, so its gradient represents the overall change in displacement divided by the total time interval, which is the average velocity. A tangent touches the curve at a single point, so its gradient represents the rate of change of displacement at that exact instant, which is the instantaneous velocity.
teacher_walkthrough: Award 1 mark for connecting the secant line to overall displacement over elapsed time (average velocity).
Award 1 mark for connecting the tangent to the rate of change at a single instant (instantaneous velocity).
